NREL and HPE will collaborate to add Artificial Intelligence (AI) to NREL’s real-time data collection/ aggregation/ streaming system and HPE’s Data Monitoring/ Management System, with the goal of improving the operational efficiency of NREL’s Energy Systems Integration Facility (ESIF) HPC Data Center through data analytics on both historical and real-time data from IT systems and facilities operations. This collaboration will consist of efforts in Data Management, Data Analytics, and AI/ML Optimization for both manual and autonomous intervention in data center operations. This will be a multi-year, multi-staged effort with a goal towards building capabilities for an Advanced Smart Facility, and demonstration of these techniques in the NREL ESIF HPC Data Center. CRADA benefit to DOE, Participant, and US Taxpayer: • Adds new capability to the laboratory’s core competencies, and/or • Uses the laboratory’s core competencies Task Descriptions 3.1 Year 1: Basic “Smart Facility” In Year 1, the team will be focused on the following high-level tasks: • Establishing data resources necessary to enable the Smart Facility • Facility operation and optimization • Predictive analytics for preventative maintenance 3.1.1 Data Resources for the Smart Facility This task will focus on establishing the data resources needed to drive effective decision-making for efficient operations and optimization of the data center. Specifically, we will work to establish: • Available data streams that can be leveraged for the data analytics • Creation of new data streams from the HPC systems and Facilities, also to be leveraged for data analytics • Integration and aggregation methods needed to provide an accessible data layer • Initial statistical models to verify correlations and establish baseline predictive measures 3.1.2 Facility Operation and Optimization This task will focus on the operation and optimization of the mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) infrastructure. Specifically, NREL and HPE will first focus on the PUE metric as follows: • Investigate data trends and predictive potential for the PUE. • Investigate relationships of the PUE calculated result to other available metrics. 2 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Resources permitting during Year 1 apply results to additional metrics, such as: • WUE • Waste heat re-capture and re-use via ERE (Energy Re-Use Effectiveness) • Facility power consumption in response to impending weather 3.1.3 Predictive Analytics and Preventative Maintenance This task will focus on establishing metrics and potential targets for predictive analytics for preventative maintenance. NREL and HPE will explore methods of using results of at least one metric to schedule preventative maintenance. Example focus areas for targets include: • Memory performance, e.g., soft errors • Device temperatures and sensor drift, e.g., for CPUs, GPUs, etc. • Disk failures • Facility pumps and their operation/performance 3.2 Year 2: Intermediate “Smart Facility” In Year 2, the team will be focused on the following high-level tasks: • Predictive scheduling of cooling • Instrumentation resiliency, integrity, and anomaly detection 3.2.1 Predictive Scheduling of Cooling NREL uses a system from Delta for its cooling infrastructure.
